When requested to rate their experiences of balancing their personal and professional lives on a scale of 1-10 (1 being "impossible to maintain" and 10 being "extremely easy to maintain"), most respondents (66%) chose a rating of 5 or less. ConclusionThis study supports previous findings that physician-parents face a myriad of challenges integrating their roles in medicine and parenthood. A change in culture is required to support and normalize parenthood for physicians and foster sustainability and productivity in academic medicine.

items.title_en: Inhalation exposure to methamphetamine in contaminated residences
items.title_zh: 污染住宅中甲基苯丙胺的吸入暴露
items.abstract_en: Current health risk assessments from thirdhand exposure to methamphetamine (meth) to occupants of contaminated residences when no cooking or use is still occurring assume that inhalation exposure is insignificant. After Wright et al. (2021) reported substantial meth concentrations in a contaminated residence, the present study was conducted to further test the hypothesis that concentrations were high enough to contribute to total occupant dose. Air sampling was conducted in contaminated residences that had been previously sampled for surface contamination. Samples were collected on personal sampling pumps in fixed locations on treated glass fiber filters is cassettes and analyzed by gas or liquid chromatography with mass spectroscopy. Sixty-nine samples were collected from eighteen residences for the study. Meth concentrations ranged from 0.02 to 15 ug/m3. Concentrations in supply air vents were significantly higher than in return vents or in ambient air. Residences with no HVAC systems (baseboard heat) had airborne concentrations similar to residences with HVAC systems turned off, and lower than when HVAC was on. Whether a residence was occupied or not did not show differences. All data from residences with HVAC had a significant correlation with surface concentrations (R2 = 0.61) but some factors that affected results were not determined in the study. In the context of the risk assessment and regulatory standard established by California and adopted in several other states, the inhalation exposure would approximately double total occupant dose for infants, and this population would exceed the California reference dose by approximately 100%. Further studies should be conducted to refine these estimates and determine the factors that influence airborne concentrations.

items.title_en: Cardiometabolic stress induces atrial myopathy in mice, characterized by structural remodelling, metabolic dysfunction, and incomplete transcriptional recovery.
items.title_zh: 心脏代谢应激诱导小鼠心房肌病，其特征为结构重塑、代谢功能障碍和转录恢复不完全
items.abstract_en: Background: The mechanisms underlying atrial remodelling and recovery following the withdrawal of cardiometabolic stress remain incompletely understood. We investigated the functional, metabolic, and transcriptional consequences of metabolic-hypertensive stress (MHS), a murine model of cardiometabolic HFpEF, in the left atrium (LA) and assessed the reversibility of these alterations following myocardial recovery. Methods and Results: Male and female mice underwent a two-hit HFpEF-inducing protocol consisting of angiotensin II infusion and a high-fat diet combined with physical inactivity (metabolic-hypertensive stress, MHS). Following 4 weeks of MHS, mice underwent a 4-week myocardial recovery (MR) phase involving stress withdrawal, dietary normalization, and voluntary exercise. We assessed LA function by speckle-tracking echocardiography, mitochondrial respiration by high-resolution respirometry, and transcriptomic remodelling by bulk RNA sequencing. MHS markedly reduced LA reservoir, conduit, and contractile strain, consistent with atrial myopathy. Transcriptomic analyses revealed substantially greater remodelling in the LA than previously observed in the left ventricle under comparable experimental conditions. Hallmark pathway analysis showed activation of extracellular matrix remodelling and profibrotic signalling pathways, along with suppression of oxidative phosphorylation and fatty acid metabolism. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a structural remodelling module enriched for extracellular matrix organization and angiogenesis pathways, as well as a bioenergetic module enriched for mitochondrial respiratory functions. Although inflammatory and structural remodelling pathways largely normalized following myocardial recovery, mitochondrial and metabolic programs exhibited incomplete restoration. Persistent transcriptional alterations were concentrated within a stress-responsive gene network enriched for adaptive cellular response pathways. In parallel, a discrete regulatory module displayed significant sex-dependent expression patterns. Conclusions: Metabolic-hypertensive stress induces profound atrial functional, metabolic, and transcriptomic remodelling, consistent with the development of cardiometabolic atrial myopathy. While many stress-induced changes resolve following myocardial recovery, key bioenergetic and stress-responsive transcriptional programs persist, suggesting that cardiometabolic stress leaves a lasting molecular imprint within the atrium.

items.title_en: RNA-seq analysis of Triatoma gerstaeckeri during mite infestation reveals increased metabolic demand and lower reproductive investment
items.title_zh: 螨侵染期间Triatoma gerstaeckeri的RNA-seq分析揭示代谢需求增加和繁殖投入降低
items.abstract_en: Triatomine insects, also known as kissing bugs, serve as vectors for the Trypanosoma cruzi parasite, which can cause American trypanosomiasis, also known as Chagas disease. Triatomines are known to be parasitized by mites in natural and colony settings, where mites feed on the arthropod to obtain nutrients and resources for reproduction. This feeding, while necessary for the survival of the mites, likely occurs at the expense of their insect host. We examined the transcriptional response of Triatoma gerstaeckeri infested with mites (Pimeliaphilus spp.) and an uninfested group using Illumina-based RNA-seq, followed by targeted measurement of nutritional reserves in both groups. Our results show increased expression of factors involved in protein translation, but decreased expression of processes associated with cell development. These results are supported by declines in protein levels in mite-infested T. gerstaeckeri and lower expression of reproductive factors, suggesting a distinct reduction in nutrient reserves and reproductive output. These studies provide critical information on the interaction of mites and triatomines while considering the utility of mites as biological control of triatomines in nature or for husbandry protocols to minimize issues with mite infestations of colony individuals.

items.title_en: A Reproducible Cortical Model of Focal Epileptiform Activity with a Multi-Biomarker Analysis Pipeline
items.title_zh: 具有多生物标志物分析流程的局灶性癫痫样活动可重复皮层模型
items.abstract_en: The development of surface-based therapeutic strategies, including extracranial illumination and epicortical electrical or optoelectronic neuromodulation, requires experimental models in which focal pathological activity can be generated and monitored within an accessible cortical region. Here, we established an acute cortical model of focal epileptiform activity in anesthetized mice based on local microinjection of 4-aminopyridine (4-AP) into the barrel cortex. This preparation provides precise spatial and temporal control of the epileptiform focus while enabling simultaneous electrophysiological sampling across cortical depth. To objectively characterize the induced activity, we implemented a Python-based analysis pipeline integrating complementary electrophysiological biomarkers, including oscillatory power, multi-unit activity, pathological fast ripples (250-650 Hz), and epileptiform bursts. Local 4-AP administration produced robust increases in gamma (30-100 Hz) power, multi-unit firing (MUA), fast ripple and burst activity. Pharmacological sensitivity of the framework was evaluated using carbamazepine, which robustly attenuated 4-AP-induced increases in all biomarkers. Together, this study provides a reproducible experimental and analytical framework for investigating focal cortical epileptiform activity and for the future evaluation of pharmacological, optical, and electrical interventions targeting superficial cortical networks.

items.title_en: The role of world knowledge in sentence comprehension under working-memory constraints: An fMRI study
items.title_zh: 工作记忆约束下世界知识在句子理解中的作用：一项fMRI研究
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Comprehension of thematic roles, i.e., "who did what to whom," relies on limited cognitive resources, and constraints on these resources can alter the use of plausibility information derived from world knowledge. Although sentence-processing studies have described how plausibility information constrains interpretation, it remains unclear how this process is supported by the architecture of working memory. This study examines whether the phonological loop, one of the components of working memory, contributes to thematic-role processing based on world knowledge. Methods: Using articulatory suppression and functional magnetic resonance imaging, we examined whether constraining the function of the phonological loop modulates behavioral and neural responses to sentences in which syntactically assigned thematic roles are plausible or implausible given world knowledge. To constrain the phonological loop, we manipulated the task: a single task and a dual task involving concurrent articulation. Results: We found no significant interaction between task and plausibility, although equivalence analyses did not provide evidence for the absence of a plausibility effect during articulation. In contrast, a robust main effect of thematic-role plausibility was observed: implausible sentences elicited greater activation than plausible sentences in the left inferior frontal gyrus (LIFG) and medial superior frontal gyrus (mSFG) at the whole-brain level, and in both the pars triangularis and pars orbitalis of the LIFG in the ROI analyses. Discussion: These findings provide no conclusive evidence that constraining the phonological loop substantially modulates the use of world knowledge in comprehension of thematic roles, while also leaving open the possibility of a smaller task-dependent effect. At the same time, the robust neural responses to implausibility indicate that the LIFG and mSFG consistently contribute to the processing of plausibility information derived from world knowledge.

items.title_en: Stemness overcomes IFNγ-induced antitumour exhaustion in human macrophages
items.title_zh: 干性克服人巨噬细胞中IFNγ诱导的抗肿瘤耗竭
items.abstract_en: Macrophages hold great promise for antitumour therapies (1-4), particularly owing to their ability to infiltrate solid tumours (5). Yet therapeutic success has been limited (6,7), because macrophages exhibit rapid exhaustion of antitumorigenic activity in the tumour (5,8,9). Here, we induced a stem-like self-renewal programme in human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived macrophages by deleting the self-renewal restricting transcription factors MAFB and MAF (MAF-DKO). Human MAF-DKO macrophages showed activated stem cell signatures, increased clonogenicity and proliferative potential. Increased self-renewal capacity was accompanied by enhanced mitochondrial fitness and invigorated energy metabolism. Importantly, these stemness features prevented exhaustion, cellular aging-associated parameters and loss of energy efficiency that are typically associated with proinflammatory macrophage activation. In addition, activated MAF-DKO macrophages showed a broad loss of IFN{gamma}-triggered immunosuppressive pathways (10,11), induced a super-activated state with robust cytotoxic activity and resisted exhaustion upon tumour cell exposure. Consequently, activated MAF-DKO macrophages showed intratumoral persistence with a stable antitumoral phenotype in vivo, conferred robust reduction of tumour burden and extended survival of tumour-bearing mice. Together, this demonstrates that the induction of stemness in human macrophages can overcome critical roadblocks of antitumour therapy by conferring resistance to activation-triggered exhaustion of antitumour activity in the TME.

items.title_en: Bacteriophage susceptibility in clinical Enterococcus faecalis reflects host genomic background and Epa-associated phage adsorption
items.title_zh: 临床粪肠球菌的噬菌体敏感性反映宿主基因组背景和Epa相关噬菌体吸附
items.abstract_en: Cytolysin-positive Enterococcus faecalis has been implicated as a disease-associated pathobiont in alcohol-associated hepatitis, motivating development of selective bacteriophage-based strategies. However, strain-level determinants of phage susceptibility remain incompletely understood. We characterized the host range of three E. faecalis phages, {Phi}Ef2.1, {Phi}Ef2.2, and {Phi}Ef2.3Ev, across 45 clinical isolates and investigated bacterial and phage factors associated with adsorption and productive infection. Isolates were characterized by whole-genome sequencing, cytolysin status, antimicrobial resistance determinants, and predicted anti-phage defense systems. Phage susceptibility was measured by efficiency of plating (EoP) and adsorption assays. Thirty-five of the 45 isolates (77.8%), including all 15 cylLs-positive isolates, were susceptible to at least one of the three phages at EoP [≥]0.01. {Phi}Ef2.1 and {Phi}Ef2.2 showed greater activity against cylLs-positive isolates, which also carried higher burdens of predicted antimicrobial resistance determinants and anti-phage defense system types. Analysis of 367 complete E. faecalis RefSeq genomes classified the variable region of the enterococcal polysaccharide antigen (epa) locus into 15 recurrent architecture groups that were associated with phage-specific adsorption patterns. Efficient adsorption did not always result in productive infection, indicating additional post-adsorption barriers. AbiD emerged as a candidate factor associated with reduced {Phi}Ef2.2 productivity, although this signal was prediction-tool dependent, while unexplained post-adsorption blocks suggest the involvement of additional uncharacterized mechanisms. These findings link naturally occurring epa architecture to phage adsorption and highlight distinct post-adsorption constraints on host range, providing a framework for rational phage selection against clinically relevant E. faecalis populations.

items.title_en: Root exudates enhance the ecological fitness of a non-native PGPR and reshape rhizosphere microbiome assembly
items.title_zh: 根系分泌物增强非本土PGPR的生态适合度并重塑根际微生物组组装
items.abstract_en: Root exudates play critical roles in rhizosphere microbiome assembly. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms by which plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) perceive these signals, adapt to the rhizosphere, and influence native microbial communities remain poorly understood. Here, using maize (Zea mays cv. Early Golden Bantam) and the rhizobacterium Priestia aryabhattai AB211, we took a multi-omics approach combining metabolomics, bacterial transcriptomics and proteomics, and rhizosphere metagenomics to elucidate the mechanism underlying this process. Maize root exudates were enriched in diverse carbon and nitrogen metabolites that promoted bacterial growth and induced extensive molecular reprogramming of pathways involved in nutrient acquisition, chemotaxis, motility, stress adaptation, and plant growth promotion, thereby enhancing rhizosphere competence. In field-conditioned soil, AB211 persisted as a core member of the maize rhizosphere microbiome, promoted early seedling growth, and reshaped microbial community composition and function. Root exudates-primed (RE-primed) AB211 further enhanced the enrichment of microbial functions associated with nutrient cycling, quorum sensing, plant growth promotion, and rhizosphere fitness, highlighting the role of root exudates in modulating the rhizosphere-adaptative potential of beneficial bacteria. These findings establish a mechanistic framework linking root exudates composition with PGPR adaptation and microbiome assembly, providing a foundation for engineering ecologically adapted microbial inoculants to improve crop productivity and sustainable agriculture.

items.title_en: A silent intergenic locus for efficient and versatile transgene expression in Plasmodium falciparum
items.title_zh: 恶性疟原虫中用于高效且通用转基因表达的沉默基因间位点
items.abstract_en: Genetically modified Plasmodium falciparum parasites expressing transgenes such as fluorescent markers are crucial tools for malaria research. However, current reporter lines often rely on integrated transgene constructs that disrupt the coding sequence of a native gene, potentially affecting progression in the life cycle of the tool parasite line. We identified six candidate Silent Intergenic Loci (SILs): putatively editable intergenic regions without transcriptional activity, where gene insertions occurred in P. falciparum after its divergence from Plasmodium berghei and Plasmodium vivax. We characterised the largest candidate SIL on chromosome 12, SIL12, by integration of a constitutively expressed cytosolic mScarlet reporter. The resulting PfRed12 parasites progressed normally throughout the life cycle, from asexual blood-stage replication to mosquito stages and subsequent liver infection. Importantly, they infected both Anopheles stephensi and Anopheles coluzzii mosquitoes. PfRed12 parasites displayed bright fluorescence in both blood and mosquito stages, making them well suited for live visualisation of parasite transmission. In addition, we used two CRISPR-Cas9 target sites in the mScarlet cassette, one of which we purposely added, to perform efficient re-editing of the transgene. As a proof of concept, we re-edited PfRed12 parasites and integrated an apicoplast metabolic bypass construct, an inducible gametocyte producer construct, and two mNeonGreen reporter constructs. Together, our findings demonstrate that SIL12 permits stable transgene expression without compromising parasite development throughout the life cycle. We established PfRed12 as a new reporter line to study blood- and mosquito-stage development and as a versatile parental line for further genetic engineering.

items.title_en: Genomic and physiological characterization of Neobacillus ammoniipjilus sp. nov. reveals versatile inorganic nitrogen utilization and ammonia-mitigation potential
items.title_zh: 新种 Neobacillus ammoniipjilus 的基因组与生理学表征揭示其多样化的无机氮利用及氨减排潜力
items.abstract_en: A novel bacterial strain (KR4-4T), was isolated from soil in the Republic of Korea and subjected to polyphasic taxonomic and functional characterization. Phylogenetic analysis based on the 16S rRNA gene sequence placed strain KR4-4T within the genus Neobacillus. Phylogenomic analysis based on 92 bacterial core genes further supported its distinct taxonomic position. Average nucleotide identity and digital DNA-DNA hybridization values between KR4-4T and related Neobacillus type strains were 69.76-82.31% and 18.3-25.9%, respectively, supporting its recognition as a distinct species. Cells were Gram-stain-positive, non-motile, facultatively anaerobic rods, with growth occurring at 15-45 {degrees}C, pH 6.0-8.0, and 0-2.0% (w/v) NaCl. The major cellular fatty acids were iso-C15:0 and anteiso-C15:0, while the major polar lipids included diphosphatidylglycerol, phosphatidylglycerol, and phosphatidylethanolamine. Genome analysis revealed genes associated with inorganic nitrogen transport, nitrate and nitrite reduction, and ammonium assimilation. In liquid culture, KR4-4T removed NH4+-N under aerobic conditions and was able to utilize ammonium, nitrate, and nitrite as individual nitrogen sources, with removal efficiencies of 86.5%, 69.35%, and 62.9%, respectively. The strain also contributed to the reduction of gaseous NH3 in a closed-flask assay. Together, these physiological and genomic characteristics indicate a versatile capacity for inorganic nitrogen utilization and transformation and suggest potential for further evaluation in biological ammonia-mitigation applications. Based on phylogenetic, genomic, phenotypic, and chemotaxonomic evidence, strain KR4-4T represents a novel species of the genus Neobacillus, for which the name Neobacillus ammoniiphilus sp. nov. is proposed. The type strain is KR4-4T (= KACC 24003T = CCTCC AB 2025077T).

items.title_en: Quantitative host-response mapping enables phenotypic profiling of viruses detected by virome sequencing
items.title_zh: 定量宿主反应图谱支持对病毒组测序所检测病毒进行表型分析
items.abstract_en: Animal-derived viruses have repeatedly caused human outbreaks, motivating efforts to identify and characterize viruses circulating in animals. Virome sequencing has accelerated animal virus discovery, but phenotypic characterization remains difficult to scale. Although generated for viral detection, virome RNA-seq data also capture host transcriptional responses to infection. Here, we developed ViroChart, a comparative transcriptomic framework that quantifies activities across biological pathways and maps diverse mammalian host responses into a common, interpretable low-dimensional space. ViroChart enables clustering of infected samples by host response pattern and quantitative assessment of host response similarity between samples. In virome data sets from wild and farmed animals, some lung samples infected with poorly characterized betacoronaviruses showed host responses resembling those induced by viruses capable of causing fatal disease. ViroChart also revealed host-response heterogeneity in natural infections: among rats with zoonotic rodent-borne viruses, most showed weak responses, consistent with asymptomatic infection, but some showed pronounced inflammation characteristic of acute infection. ViroChart thus enables phenotypic characterization and prioritization of newly detected viruses by leveraging the same RNA-seq data from which their genomes were detected.

items.title_en: Concentration-dependent inhibition of Streptococcus mutans metabolic activity by purified Croton lechleri latex (sangre de grado) in vitro
items.title_zh: 体外条件下纯化的 Croton lechleri 乳汁（sangre de grado）对变形链球菌代谢活性的浓度依赖性抑制
items.abstract_en: Background. Chlorhexidine is the reference chemical antiplaque agent, but its adverse effects motivate the search for plant-derived alternatives. The proanthocyanidin-rich latex of Croton lechleri (sangre de grado) is a candidate, yet quantitative concentration-response data against Streptococcus mutans are scarce. Methods. In this exploratory in vitro study, ethanol-purified C. lechleri latex was tested at working concentrations of 3-100% v/v (final in-well concentrations 0.6-20% v/v) against S. mutans ATCC 25175 in a 96-well resazurin assay with dual-wavelength reading (570/600 nm) and correction for medium and latex color. Chlorhexidine 1% (0.2% in-well) was the positive control. Each condition was run in technical triplicate within a single experiment. Data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA, Tukey's test with simultaneous 95% confidence intervals (CI) and four-parameter logistic regression. Results. Metabolic activity decreased monotonically with concentration, from 101.3 +/- 1.7% (vehicle) to 54.0 +/- 4.7% (12%), 15.5 +/- 4.0% (50%) and 8.6 +/- 7.7% (100%), compared with 3.1 +/- 2.8% for chlorhexidine (F(7,16) = 160.7, p < 0.001). The lowest concentration that differed from the vehicle was 6% (difference 17.6 percentage points, 95% CI 2.1-33.1). The estimated half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) was 12.3% v/v (95% CI 9.5-15.1). Differences from chlorhexidine at 50% and 100% were not statistically significant, but their confidence intervals were compatible with differences of up to 28 and 21 percentage points, respectively. Conclusions. Purified C. lechleri latex inhibited the metabolic activity of planktonic S. mutans in a concentration-dependent manner. These preliminary findings do not establish equivalence with chlorhexidine and warrant replication in independent experiments with chemically standardized extracts expressed in mg/mL, determination of MIC/MBC and biofilm models.

items.title_en: Cardioselective β-blocker Therapy Resolves Staphylococcus aureus Toxin-Induced Innate Immunoparalysis
items.title_zh: 心脏选择性β受体阻滞剂治疗可逆转金黄色葡萄球菌毒素诱导的固有免疫麻痹
items.abstract_en: During Staphylococcus aureus sepsis, the pore-forming -toxin (Hla) triggers lytic platelet death and provokes the release of catecholamines that modulate leukocyte effector function. The resulting surge in catecholaminergic action paralyzes host antimicrobial capacity by upregulating interleukin-10 (IL-10), profoundly suppressing the protective interferon (IFN) response to orchestrate innate immunoparalysis. Here, we deconvolute a multi-cellular regulatory pathway in the blood and highlight a pivotal immunological checkpoint, where pharmacological intervention with cardioselective {beta}-blockers uncouples the immunosuppressive cascade, restores host antimicrobial function, and significantly improves survival outcomes.

items.title_en: Pan-cancer estimation of prognostic immune biomarkers from histopathology using artificial intelligence
items.title_zh: 利用人工智能从组织病理学中泛癌评估预后免疫生物标志物
items.abstract_en: Multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) assays such as ImmunoProfile provide standardized quantification of prognostic immune markers but are costly and not routinely used in clinical settings. We developed a weakly-supervised AI model, HistoProfile, to estimate intratumoral cell densities of key immune biomarkers (CD8, FOXP3, PD-1, and PD-L1) and the PD-L1 tumor proportion score from routine H&E-stained whole-slide images. Trained on a large pan-cancer cohort with paired H&E and mIF data, HistoProfile discriminated biomarker-high from biomarker-low tumors in held-out samples and tumor-specific subgroups (AUROCs of 0.78-0.89 across biomarkers). Critically, the estimated biomarkers preserved prognostic stratification in downstream survival analyses, and showed cancer-specific survival associations across TCGA cohorts where mIF is unavailable. These findings support scalable H&E-based estimation of key immune biomarker measurements for large-scale immune profiling and risk stratification.

items.title_en: ALBIS: simulation of multi-resolution and multi-dimensional spatial transcriptomics data
items.title_zh: ALBIS：多分辨率与多维空间转录组数据的模拟
items.abstract_en: The rapid adoption of spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies has been accompanied by substantial growth in computational methods, creating an increasing need for systematic and reliable benchmarking, particularly as analyses increasingly extend from individual tissue sections to three-dimensional (3D) tissue reconstruction. Existing benchmarks often rely on a small and similar set of experimentally-derived datasets because they offer a reliable ground truth label, which is hard to find in practice. Simulated or synthetic data provide an alternative, yet most existing simulators either adapt single-cell RNA-sequencing models to spatial coordinates or generate individual sections in a two-dimensional (2D) space at predefined resolutions. More recent approaches can simulate 2D and 3D tissues, but generally do not derive multiple spatial resolutions from the same molecular realization. Here, we introduce ALBIS (A muLti-resolution Biological In-silico Simulator for spatial transcriptomics), a statistically grounded and highly customizable framework that generates synthetic ST data from an in silico 3D tissue. ALBIS defines spatially structured cell populations with corresponding markers for gene expression, then initializes individual mRNA molecules in 3D space to create cell-level information with a ground truth 3D coordinate for each molecule and cell. From this common realization, ALBIS cuts the 3D tissue into multiple 2D tissue sections with cell-, bin-, and spot-level measurements, enabling direct comparison across spatial resolutions. Properties of the simulated data, including spatial domains, cell type composition, gene-expression effects, batch effects, measurement resolution, and tissue scale, can be systematically varied, enabling rigorous stress-testing of computational methods under known and increasingly challenging conditions.

items.title_en: Lack of adoption of computational gene-panel-selection tools in targeted spatial transcriptomics
items.abstract_en: Targeted spatial transcriptomics requires selecting a gene panel before any experiment is run. Choosing well across tens of thousands of candidate genes under platform-specific probe, panel-size, and sensitivity constraints is difficult to do manually, and impossible to correct once a panel has been used. A growing number of computational tools to automate this selection have been designed, yet it remains unclear whether they are adopted in practice. Several factors could limit uptake: validation uncertainty about panel performance, workflow friction between a ranked gene list and a submission-ready panel, limited platform awareness in tools developed for dissociated single-cell data, and the cost advantage of vendor panels. We analyzed 18 computational tools for gene-panel selection from two angles: their citation landscape and their use across a targeted spatial transcriptomics corpus. Across 540 full-text-classified records, only 35 (6.5%) reported using the cited tool for panel design; most came from computational, benchmark, review, or non-spatial papers, or papers that cited but did not use it. In an independent corpus, only 34 of 479 (7.1%) involved a computational tool, alone or in a hybrid workflow; most used manually curated, premade vendor, or modified vendor panels. Both lines of evidence point the same way: computational selection is rarely part of the reported experimental workflow, and it more often supplemented manual curation than replaced it. Adoption is unlikely to turn on further benchmark gains alone; it will depend on reducing the validation uncertainty and workflow friction that keep users on established panel-design practice.

items.title_en: Interlaboratory benchmarking of differential scanning fluorimetry reveals sources of variability in protein thermal stability parameters
items.abstract_en: Differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF) is widely used to assess protein thermal stability and to compare protein variants, ligands, or formulations with limited sample consumption. Yet, the reproducibility of DSF derived parameters across laboratories, instruments and analysis workflows remains poorly defined. Here, we report a two phase interlaboratory benchmark using a shared VHH sample across 26 laboratories, 28 instruments and seven DSF instrument models. In Phase 1, participants applied their routine acquisition and analysis workflows, whereas in Phase 2, acquisition conditions were harmonised. Datasets were analysed locally and then centrally reprocessed with MoltenProt. Participant reported apparent melting temperatures (Tm) showed good within instrument repeatability but moderate inter instrument dispersion. Harmonisation of acquisition conditions did not substantially reduce this dispersion. Conversely, centralised reprocessing narrowed the distribution among retained datasets, indicating contributions from analysis workflows and data acceptance criteria in addition to instrument dependent factors. Comparison with differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further showed that apparent Tm depended strongly on the fluorescence readout. For this VHH, single wavelength fluorescence at 350 nm showed the closest agreement with the DSC transition temperature, whereas the 350/330 nm ratio and barycentric mean generally yielded higher values. Furthermore, DSF derived apparent unfolding enthalpies were more variable than apparent Tm. Together, these findings show that DSF can be highly repeatable within a defined instrument and workflow, but that quantitative comparability across instruments depends on instrument specific effects, the choice of fluorescence readout and analysis strategy. Improved comparability will require transparent reporting of acquisition and analysis conditions, explicit data quality criteria, and well characterised reference materials to monitor instrument dependent offsets.

items.title_en: An inspectable Grover algorithm-based amplitude-amplification workflow for k-mer discovery and motif scanning with genomic coordinate traceability
items.abstract_en: Motif discovery and motif scanning remain core primitives in genomics, but both tasks face combinatorial growth as k-mer length increases and as mismatch-tolerant searches expand the candidate space. In this work, we present MotifQu, a Python package and command-line tool that maps two common motif-analysis workflows-(i) scanning a genome for a user-specified consensus motif and (ii) de novo discovery of recurrent k-mers above a user-defined count threshold-onto Grover-style amplitude amplification circuits executed reproducibly via Qiskit Aer statevector simulation. We evaluate MotifQu on the SARS-CoV-2 reference contig (29,903 bp) and S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome, where the classical census identifies strongly non-uniform motif frequencies dominated by A/T-rich 5-mers and returns explicit coordinate lists across the full genome span. We further execute the same logical 10-qubit search on IBM hardware showing that while end-to-end execution is feasible, transpilation-induced circuit depth and entangling-gate volume produce a diffuse measurement distribution whose probabilities remain close to the uniform 1/1024 scale, limiting observable amplitude concentration under current NISQ constraints. Finally, we demonstrate the full discovery workflow on the S. cerevisiae S288C reference genome (12,157,105 bp) to illustrate search results (ranked motifs, probability summaries, circuit diagrams, and position plots) and to highlight the regime where a large, marked set reduces the sharpness of Grover amplification.

items.title_en: Genomic Profiling of Estrogen-Related Receptor Identifies Adult Adipocyte-Specific Targets in Drosophila
items.abstract_en: Adipose tissue is a key metabolic organ for carbohydrate and lipid metabolism. Multiple nutrient sensing pathways and metabolic enzymes operate in adipocytes to control energy production and lipid mobilization in response to physiological conditions. Important regulators of glycolytic and lipid metabolism in many species are members of the estrogen-related receptor (ERR) family of nuclear receptors. We previously showed that ERR is required for transcriptional regulation of glycolytic and pentose phosphate pathway enzymes in adult Drosophila females, consistent with what is observed in ERR mutant males and larvae. However, the cell-type specific targets of ERR in adipose and other tissues have not been fully elucidated. Here, using a modified targeted DamID approach (NanoDam), we identified ERR occupancy specifically in adult adipocytes at the loci that encode genes involved in glycolysis, the pentose phosphate pathway, and fatty acid metabolism. Overall, our results predict that ERR centrally functions in adipose tissue to regulate multiple metabolic pathways.

items.title_en: Increases in therapist-patient physiological synchrony after dog-patient contact in canine-assisted psychotherapy: an exploratory pilot study
items.abstract_en: Introduction: Canine-assisted psychotherapy (CAP) introduces a therapy dog into the therapist-patient relationship and may influence interpersonal processes underlying therapeutic change. This exploratory pilot study investigated whether direct patient-dog contact is associated with changes in autonomic arousal and therapist-patient physiological synchrony. Methods: Skin conductance was recorded from 18 patients with depressive disorders and one therapist during 53 routine CAP sessions. A total of 192 episodes of direct patient-dog contact were identified from video recordings. Three-minute periods before and after each contact onsets were compared. Skin conductance level (SCL), skin conductance fluctuations (SCF), and therapist-patient physiological synchrony were assessed using zero-lag correlation and maximum cross-correlation. Sliding-window analyses examined temporal changes in synchrony, while randomly selected pseudo-events served as controls. Results: SCL increased significantly following dog contact in both patients and the therapist, whereas SCF rate over 3 min did not change significantly. Therapist-patient physiological synchrony increased significantly after dog contact, as indicated by both zero-lag correlation and maximum cross-correlation. Sliding-window analyses confirmed these increases and showed a reduction in the temporal lag between the two physiological signals. Importantly, increases in synchrony were significantly greater following genuine dog-contact events than following pseudo-events. Discussion: Direct physical contact between patients and therapy dogs is followed by increased autonomic arousal and enhanced therapist-patient physiological synchrony. These findings suggest that dog-patient contact may function as an interactional event that promotes physiological coordination and interpersonal attunement within the therapeutic dyad.

items.title_en: Rapid Emergence of an Adaptive Spatial Representation
items.abstract_en: Peripheral sensory cue availability fluctuates across timescales ranging from seconds to years. This requires central circuits to continuously adapt their representations while preserving established codes, but how the brain achieves this flexibility is unknown. Using two-photon calcium imaging in the mouse inferior colliculus, we address this knowledge gap by testing how neurons encode sound location before and after abruptly disrupting binaural cues via monaural hearing loss. Despite measurable single neuron changes, altering binaural cues had remarkably little impact on the encoding of auditory space. Rather, neural activity rotated into a spatially informative representational subspace, orthogonal to the original binaural axis, within two hours of hearing loss. This rotation occurred in absence of overt experience or training, and reflected a shift from ON- to OFF-dominated spatial selectivity. Thus, central population codes rapidly reorganize to accommodate sudden changes at the periphery, without overwriting existing representations.

items.title_en: Seeing at Will: Shared Neural Representations of Motion Perception and Intention
items.abstract_en: Intention can bias perception in cases where two or more interpretations of a stimulus are possible. The neural mechanisms whereby intention influences perception are poorly understood. Here we investigated whether the intention to perceive horizontal or vertical motion in a bistable apparent motion stimulus pre-activates motion axes representations in sensory cortex before the position shift occurs and before motion in consciously perceived. Twelve participants underwent fMRI scanning under three conditions: (1) passively viewing quartet stimuli moving continuously along veridical trajectories; (2) passively viewing bistable apparent motion quartet stimuli induced by two pairs of squares alternately flashing at diagonally opposite corners of an invisible rectangle; or (3) while actively intending to perceive a single-shot apparent-motion stimulus as moving either vertically or horizontally. Multivariate decoding analyses revealed that activity patterns during the intention period of (3) generalized to patterns evoked by both (1) physical and (2) ambiguous motion perception. Cross-decoding was strongest within dorsal/lateral visual regions, including hMT+, V3AB, and the intraparietal sulcus, but was largely absent from ventral visual cortex. Widespread overlap was also observed between intention-related and perceptual motion representations throughout the dorsal/lateral visual cortex. Our findings suggest that intention may bias prospective sensory representations prior to the stimulus-driven processing that results in perceptual experience and that these representations closely resemble those associated with illusory motion perception. The fact that intention-related representations were mostly found within dorsal/lateral visual regions is consistent with top-down influences from attentional control systems.

items.title_en: ASC specks and α-synuclein amplify microglial NLRP3 inflammasome activation and co-localize with Lewy body pathology
items.abstract_en: Neuroinflammation is a hallmark of several chronic neurodegenerative disorders, including Parkinson's disease (PD) and other synucleinopathies, and is closely associated with microglial activation. The inflammasome adaptor protein apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a caspase activation and recruitment domain (ASC) undergoes oligomerization upon inflammasome activation, resulting in the formation of ASC specks. These structures are recognized by microglia as damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), thereby promoting inflammatory signaling. Recent studies have demonstrated that extracellular ASC specks associate with amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}), and that uptake of ASC-A{beta} composites by microglia amplifies pro-inflammatory responses. Although ASC specks have also been shown to potentiate -synuclein (Syn) preformed fibril-induced pathology, their interaction with monomeric Syn and their effects on inflammasome activation remain poorly understood. Here, we co-stimulated murine SIM-A9 microglia with ASC-Syn assemblies and evaluated their effects on NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Electron microscopy revealed a close association between ASC fibrils and Syn monomers. Exposure of microglia to ASC-Syn enhanced NLRP3 inflammasome activation, as evidenced by increased ASC speck formation, caspase-1 activation, and secretion of IL-1{beta} and IL-18, when compared to ASC or Syn alone. In addition, immunohistochemical analyses of post mortem brain tissue from patients with dementia with Lewy bodies demonstrated ASC expression in regions exhibiting Syn pathology and showed ASC co-localization with Syn within Lewy bodies. Collectively, these findings identify ASC-Syn assemblies as potent amplifiers of NLRP3 inflammasome signaling and suggest a mechanism through which they may contribute to sustained neuroinflammation in synucleinopathies.

items.title_en: Chromatin Acetylation Overrides Substrate Stiffness-Dependent Mechanoresponse and Lineage Specification in Human Mesenchymal Stem Cells
items.abstract_en: Human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) exhibit a stiffness dependent cellular phenotype and lineage bias. Cells on soft substrate display reduced cell spreading, less cellular traction, smaller and fewer focal adhesions and decreased actin stress fibre organization, whereas cells on stiff substrate exhibit the converse behaviour. Further, hMSCs preferentially undergo adipogenic differentiation on soft substrate and osteogenic differentiation on stiff substrate. These stiffness dependent changes are accompanied by global chromatin condensation/decondensation on soft/stiff substrates. Despite these well documented correlations, it remains unclear whether modulating chromatin condensation alone can be sufficient to reprogram stiffness dependent cellular phenotype. To answer whether chromatin organization acts as an active regulatory element in rigidity sensing, we induced chromatin condensation/decondensation in hMSCs cultured on soft/stiff polyacrylamide gels using histone deacetylase inhibitor (HDACi) and histone acetyltransferase inhibitor (HATi) respectively. We found that across conditions, phenotypic outcomes including nuclear localization of mechanosignalling protein YAP correlated strongly with chromatin compaction state rather than with substrate stiffness when the cells were presented with combination of signals. Mechanistically pharmacological inhibition of ERK phosphorylation attenuated chromatin dependent lineage specification while leaving chromatin compaction unchanged, indicating that ERK phosphorylation operates downstream of chromatin state. Collectively, these findings suggests an inside-out signalling mechanism in which chromatin compaction state reprograms the stiffness dependent mechanoresponse and fate decisions in hMSCs. Altogether, this works provides a fundamental framework for integrating mechanical and epigenetic cues in designing biomaterial microenvironment for controlling hMSCs fate in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

items.title_en: Identification of active deubiquitinases in dendritic cells under unstimulated and activated conditions.
items.abstract_en: Ubiquitination is a post-translational modification with well described roles in the regulation of immune cell function, such as dendritic cells (DCs). DCs are crucial initiators and regulators of T cell-mediated immune responses. In this study, we use activity-based probes and proteomics to systematically profile DUBs in a DC line. Using the lysate-based biotin(bio)-Ubiquitin(Ub)-propargylamide(Prg) probe and proteomics, the activity and abundance of deubiquitinases was measured in unstimulated and CpG-stimulated MutuDCs to simulate responses to bacteria. This analysis was complemented with profiling using the cell-permeable DUB activity-based probe IMP-2373. The combined analysis with bio-Ub-Prg and IMP-2373 provided insights into the dynamics of DUB activity and abundance in DCs following stimulation and identified several DUBs for further study.

items.title_en: When label-free morphology is sufficient for targeted cellular measurements
items.abstract_en: Label-free morphology captures cellular responses, but its ability to substitute for targeted cellular measurements depends on the intended use. We assess measurement sufficiency using nearly 10 million paired phase-reporter observations across 1,000 gene knockouts, 52 fluorescent reporters and 73 A549 screens. Ten predictors differed in recovery across held-out fields, genes and screens. Same-cell pairing controls identified reporter-state information beyond perturbation averages and measured covariates. Perturbation ranking often persisted despite reduced variation in predicted response magnitudes. Predictions of held-out knockout responses retained a median 79% of the strongest hits, whereas functional-term retention varied. Atlas-derived criteria identified 30 quantitative and 7 ranking proxies for a fixed ensemble, with reference reproducibility constraining interpretation. In independent primary-hepatocyte data, brightfield predictions prioritized 10 of the 11 compounds with the largest measured metabolic-activity losses among 217 held-out compounds. Measurement sufficiency therefore depends on target, predictor, context and scientific task, beyond predictive correlation alone.

items.title_en: Range-wide validation of reduced locomotor endurance in unisexual Ambystoma salamanders
items.abstract_en: Locomotor endurance is a critical physiological trait dictating terrestrial dispersal and metapopulation connectivity, especially in amphibians. The unisexual Ambystoma complex is an ancient, all-female polyploid lineage that reproduces via kleptogenesis. This unique reproductive mode creates an evolutionary mismatch between a conserved mitochondrial genome and divergent nuclear subgenomes that are taken from sympatric, sexual species. This provides a compelling system for testing the physiological limits of polyploidy and how mitonuclear dissonance and subgenome composition influence phenotypes. Previous locomotor assessments of this lineage demonstrated that polyploid salamanders display reduced locomotor endurance compared to sexual species. To overcome previous limitations in geographic sampling and sample size, we conducted standardized treadmill endurance trials on a broad geographic sampling of 102 salamanders, comparing the performance of triploid unisexual biotypes (LJJ and LLJ) directly to their sexually reproducing parental species (A. jeffersonianum and A. laterale). We found that reproductive mode significantly dictated endurance performance. Sexual species broadly outperformed unisexuals, driven by A. jeffersonianum exceeding all unisexual biotypes and A. laterale outperforming LJJ unisexuals. Within the unisexual cohort, subgenome dosage did not influence performance: LJJ individuals and LLJ individuals had similar performance.. We propose that the aerobic capacity of unisexual salamanders is limited, potentially due to mitonuclear mismatch or the biophysical constraints of increased cellular volume, but not due to the contributions of individual subgenomes. This endurance deficit is likely to restrict unisexual salamanders dispersal capabilities, leaving populations uniquely vulnerable to ongoing habitat fragmentation compared to more mobile, sexual species while potentially preventing unisexuals from driving sexual hosts locally extinct.

items.title_en: Cefazolin versus Antistaphylococcal Penicillins for Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus Bacteremia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
items.abstract_en: Purpose: To compare the efficacy and safety of intravenous cefazolin versus antistaphylococcal penicillins for the treatment of MSSA bacteremia in adults using evidence exclusively from randomized controlled trials. Methods: We searched 5 databases for RCTs comparing definitive intravenous cefazolin with ASPs (oxacillin, cloxacillin, flucloxacillin, nafcillin) in adults with MSSA bacteremia. Primary outcomes were 90-day all-cause mortality and acute kidney injury (AKI). Secondary outcomes included adverse event-related treatment discontinuation and persistent bacteremia (>72h). Dichotomous outcomes were synthesized as risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using random-effects models with Paule-Mandel estimation and Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman inference. Fixed-effect Mantel-Haenszel models were performed as sensitivity analyses. Results: Two RCTs randomized 1,656 participants (SNAP, n = 1,341; CloCeBa, n = 315), of whom 1,579 contributed to the 90-day mortality analysis. There was no statistically significant difference in 90-day mortality (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.57-1.41; I2 = 0%). Both trials favoured cefazolin for acute kidney injury, but the random-effects estimate was highly imprecise (RR 0.26, 95% CI 0.00-939,970.59; I2 = 81.7%). Treatment discontinuation also favoured cefazolin directionally, although the random-effects estimate was imprecise (RR 0.24, 95% CI 0.00-24.41; I2 = 36.2%). Microbiological outcomes were synthesized narratively because definitions and assessment time points differed between trials. Conclusion: Randomized evidence supports cefazolin as a potential definitive treatment option when adequate source control, appropriate antimicrobial dosing, and clinical monitoring can be achieved. However, the limited number of trials and imprecision in pooled estimates warrant cautious interpretation.

items.title_en: Foundation Model Artificial Intelligence for Electrocardiogram Detection of Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis
items.title_zh: 基础模型人工智能用于风湿性二尖瓣狭窄的心电图检测
items.abstract_en: Background: Rheumatic mitral stenosis (RMS) disproportionately affects low-resource settings where echocardiography is limited. We evaluated foundation model (FM) feasibility for RMS detection using limited, indirectly labeled ECGs. Methods: An ECG-FM was fine-tuned using 804 RMS-positive ECGs per fold and externally validated across clinical and wearable lead configurations. Results: Internal AUROCs were 0.89, 0.87, and 0.87, for 12-Lead, 6-Lead, and 1-Lead respectively. External AUROCs were 0.82, 0.80, and 0.77. Performance remained comparable across demographic subgroups. Conclusions: FM fine-tuning enables RMS detection using limited ICD-derived labels, supporting further evaluation of reduced-lead ECG screening and echocardiography triage in resource-constrained settings.

items.title_en: Feasibility of continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video in a hypertension clinic cohort: the BP-WAVE pilot study
items.abstract_en: Introduction. Whether the arterial pressure waveform carries structural vascular information that brachial pressure does not, and whether its shape can be read from facial video, are both uncertain, and recording a continuous pressure reference with synchronised video in a hypertension clinic has not been reported. We sought to determine whether continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video, linked to existing coronary calcium imaging, is feasible in adults attending a hypertension clinic, whether a consumer camera recovers heart rate and pulse shape in that setting, and to generate exploratory estimates of association between waveform morphology and coronary calcium. Methods. BP-WAVE is a single-site prospective observational pilot study. The primary outcome was feasibility, pre-specified as recruitment, consent, completeness of waveform recording, imaging availability and data completeness. Secondary outcomes were waveform quality, device agreement, feature extraction, and recovery of heart rate and pulse shape from video. The exploratory outcome was the Spearman correlation of 14 waveform features with the Agatston calcium score, with exact permutation p values adjusted within each family of tests. Results. Nine of ten planned participants were recorded over 12 days (median age 55 years, range 40 to 74; five women); all nine completed the recording with video and had a calcium score (median 351, range 33 to 1816). Of 4,178 detected beats, 2,965 (71%) passed quality control. Video recovered heart rate within 0.4 to 4.1 beats per minute in eight of nine participants and pulse shape above a phase-randomised noise bound in six of nine (held-out r 0.48 to 0.76). Form factor had the strongest correlation with calcium (rho -0.68, exact p 0.050, q 0.68); no feature was associated with calcium after Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment within any of the nine families of 14 tests (126 tests in all; smallest q 0.17). Conclusion. In this single-site pilot of nine adults from a hypertension clinic, continuous finger arterial pressure recording with synchronised facial video and linkage to coronary calcium was feasible, a consumer camera recovered heart rate in eight and pulse shape in six participants, and no waveform feature was associated with coronary calcium after correction for multiple testing.

items.title_en: Cardiomyocyte-Derived Cell-Free DNA in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
items.abstract_en: Introduction: In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), wall stress and subclinical myocardial injury related in part to pathological hypercontractility, which in turn are associated with worse outcomes. Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is released from cardiomyocytes (cfDNA-CM) through irreversible cellular injury and death. We investigated the feasibility of quantifying cfDNA-CM and its relationship to HCM patient characteristics. Methods: We analyzed 57 plasma samples from stable patients with HCM and 10 plasma samples from patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Plasma cfDNA was isolated from both groups. Whole genome bisulfite sequencing (WGBS) libraries were generated and sequenced with short-read sequencing. Methylation patterns were used for tissue deconvolution analysis and cell-specific cfDNA quantification. Results: Yields of cfDNA (p = 0.003) and cfDNA-CM (p = 0.002) fractions were higher in AMI controls than HCM, supporting the validity of the assay. Within the HCM cohort, the median cfDNA yield was 12.22 ng [IQR: 7.77, 18.94]. The cfDNA-CM fraction in this cohort ranged from 0% to 6.4% of total cfDNA. Higher cfDNA-CM tertiles were associated with higher body mass index (BMI, p=0.001), a greater prevalence of BMI 30 kg/m2 (p<0.001), and a higher prevalence of obstructive sleep apnea (p=0.038). No significant differences were observed in other demographic, genetic, and laboratory characteristics. Higher cfDNA-CM tertile was numerically associated with higher New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, while circulating biomarkers of wall stress (NT-proBNP) and myocardial injury (troponin) did not differ across tertiles (p=0.83 and p=0.29, respectively). Conclusion: Isolation and quantification of cfDNA as well as detection of cfDNA-CM in chronic stable patients with HCM are feasible. Higher cfDNA-CM fraction was associated with increasing BMI and cardiometabolic comorbidity burden. The absence of association with traditional circulating biomarkers suggests that cfDNA-CM may reflect a distinct domain of myocardial health, injury, and adverse remodeling.

items.title_en: Mortality in Rural and Urban Emergency and Trauma Care in the United States: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract_en: Objective: Rural hospitals in the United States have fewer specialists, fewer critical care resources, and longer transport distances than urban hospitals, yet national studies disagree on whether rural patients are more likely to die after emergency care. The goal of this study was to determine whether short-term mortality differs between rural and urban patients receiving emergency or trauma care and to estimate the size of the difference. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis reported in line with PRISMA 2020. PubMed was searched on October 11, 2026, for studies published from 2010 onward, supplemented by web searching. Eligible studies were US observational studies that compared rural with urban patients or hospitals and reported mortality after emergency or trauma care. Odds ratios (ORs) were pooled with a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs) as a sensitivity analysis. Injury and trauma studies formed the primary analysis. Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Results: Of 161 records identified, 14 studies were included and 12 were pooled. Across seven injury and trauma studies, rural setting was associated with higher odds of death (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.07-1.52), with substantial heterogeneity (I^2 = 84%; 95% prediction interval, 0.74-2.19). Across all 12 studies, the pooled OR was 1.23 (95% CI, 1.09-1.40; I^2 = 96%). With Hartung-Knapp intervals, the overall estimate remained significant (95% CI, 1.05-1.45) and the trauma estimate was borderline (95% CI, 0.99-1.64). Study estimates ranged from 0.65 to 1.97. Three pediatric trauma studies gave a consistent estimate (OR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.18-1.47; I^2 = 0%). Subgroup analyses by rurality definition, age group, and geographic scope did not explain the heterogeneity. Certainty of evidence was very low. Conclusions: In pooled US observational data, rural patients receiving emergency and trauma care had about 23% higher odds of short-term death than urban patients, most consistently among injured children. The evidence is inconsistent, rests on a single-database search with several reports assessed from abstracts only, and should be treated as preliminary. Why rural patients die more often, and at what point in the pathway from injury to definitive care, remains unanswered.

items.title_en: Approach to some data preparation problems in systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract_en: In systematic review, the measures reported by the primary studies may not always be the measures sought by the systematic review investigators. Motivated by an systematic review of interventions to reduce meat consumption, we discuss here methods to infer relative risks and confidence intervals from randomized controlled trials that reported differences, possibly in the presence of repeated measures or multiple interventions.

items.title_en: Artificial Intelligence-Based Modeling to Aid in the Identification of Genetic Conditions in Infants with Congenital Heart Disease
items.title_zh: 基于人工智能的建模辅助识别先天性心脏病婴儿的遗传状况
items.abstract_en: Background: Genetic conditions are common in congenital heart disease (CHD) and affect care, but are often missed or diagnosed late. We asked whether routine clinical data can shortlist the most likely genetic conditions. Methods: Retrospective single-center cohort of children with CHD and an echocardiogram who had either a confirmed genetic diagnosis or negative cytogenetic testing and CHD gene sequencing. Echocardiogram images and serial medical record data were added as model inputs in the order they become clinically available. Class balanced logistic regression (LR) and a multimodal deep learning fusion network were fitted to the same inputs at each step. The primary metric was balanced top-3 accuracy (correct diagnosis among the top three, averaged across conditions), with bootstrap intervals. Results: The cohort included 1,720 children (988 with common CHD-associated genetic conditions, 231 rare diagnoses, 501 negative testing). Using only inputs generated at the echocardiogram visit, LR reached a balanced top-3 accuracy 0.758 (chance 0.429). Serial records, radiology notes and ICD-10 codes, raised this to 0.809. Multimodal fusion performed similarly at each stage. With a genetic condition withheld from training, the fusion embedding placed affected children nearest to others sharing a gene group in 0.37 of cases versus 0.10 without the embedding (+0.268 [95% CI +0.242, +0.295]). Conclusions: Routine clinical data available at first echocardiogram can help identify likely genetic diagnoses, and later coded inputs ceiling. Multimodal fusion added no accuracy over LR, but places children sharing a genetic cause near one another, making nearest-neighbor retrieval informative for undiagnosed children.

items.title_en: Comparing mental health treatment outcomes for autistic and non-autistic people: a systematic review
items.abstract_en: Background: Autistic people experience substantially higher rates of mental health conditions and are overrepresented in mental health services. However, most interventions and service models have been developed for non-autistic people, and evidence is needed as to whether there are disparities in outcomes. This systematic review aimed to compare outcomes between autistic and non-autistic people receiving the same mental health interventions or services. Methods: We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251021068). We searched academic databases (MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, PubMed, CINAHL), a grey literature database (HMIC), a trial registry (ISRCTN), preprint servers (medRxiv and PsyArXiv), Google, and Google Scholar, to identify relevant papers published 01/01/1992-30/04/2026. We conducted backwards and forwards citation searching and contacted experts. Study quality was assessed using a modified Critical Appraisal Skills Programme Cohort Study Checklist and the Autism-Inclusive Research Assessment (AIRA). Data were synthesised narratively, with random effects meta-analyses where appropriate. Results: Thirty-nine studies were included, comprising 4787730 participants, assessing outcomes of psychological therapies (n = 17) and multi-component or service-level approaches (n = 22). Nearly half (46.2%) were UK-based, and under a quarter (23.1%) included people with intellectual disabilities. Ten studies (25.6%) were rated low quality, twenty-two (56.4%) medium quality, and seven (17.9%) high quality. AIRA ratings highlighted concerns about research inclusiveness for autistic people, including limited involvement of autistic people and lack of validated or adapted outcome measures. Findings varied by intervention: for some, multiple large, higher-quality studies showed less favourable outcomes for autistic people (e.g., less improvement in symptoms or functioning, or higher rates of restrictive practices or acute service use). For other interventions, comparable or mixed outcomes were found across studies, with interpretation often limited by small samples. Conclusions: Mental health treatment outcomes for autistic versus non-autistic people varied across interventions and outcome types. Where significant differences were observed, these usually showed poorer outcomes for autistic people, although they generally reflected smaller improvements rather than a lack of benefit. Action is needed to improve the accessibility and appropriateness of mental health care for autistic people, supported by more high-quality, co-produced research across a broader range of countries and service contexts.

items.title_en: In Silico Metrological Assessment of 2D ROI Sampling Error Versus Whole-Organ 3D Volumetric CT Attenuation in Hepatic Steatosis: A Multicenter Monte Carlo Simulation on 971 Scans
items.abstract_en: Purpose: To quantify the sampling error of conventional 2D regions of interest (ROIs) compared with whole-organ 3D volumetric CT attenuation for opportunistic hepatic steatosis screening, and to evaluate its dependency on intraparenchymal spatial heterogeneity. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective computational study (CLAIM-compliant), 971 abdominal CT scans were analyzed across a multicenter derivation cohort (TotalSegmentator v2, n = 841) and an external validation cohort (Medical Segmentation Decathlon Task03, n = 130). Automated 3D liver segmentation was performed using nnU-Net, followed by an 8-mm spherical 3D erosion to eliminate peripheral partial volume effects and major hilar vessels. Three clinical sampling paradigms (1, 3, and 5 axial 2D ROIs of 15 mm diameter) were modeled through 500 stochastic Monte Carlo iterations per scan (485,500 total simulations). Absolute sampling error (|Delta HU| = |HU_ROI - HU_3D|) and diagnostic misclassification rates at the standard <= 40 HU steatosis threshold were computed. Results: In the derivation cohort, the conventional 3-ROI approach yielded a mean absolute error of 6.61 +/- 7.83 HU (median: 2.92 HU), significantly underperforming compared to the 5-ROI strategy (5.21 +/- 6.00 HU; Wilcoxon paired test, p < 0.001) but improving on the single-ROI approach (11.32 +/- 14.16 HU; p < 0.001). Sampling error correlated strongly with parenchymal spatial heterogeneity (Pearson r = 0.850, 95% CI: [0.830-0.868], p < 0.001). In borderline attenuation zones (35-45 HU), diagnostic misclassification reached 45.2% in heterogeneous livers. Findings were corroborated on external validation, confirming the reproducible decay of sampling error (|Delta HU| = 7.38 HU for 1 ROI vs. 5.14 HU for 3 ROI, p < 0.001). Conclusion: Manual 2D ROI sampling exhibits an intrinsic metrological uncertainty exceeding clinically relevant thresholds (5 HU) in heterogeneous livers, misclassifying nearly half of borderline cases. Opportunistic screening requires fully automated 3D volumetric extraction embedded into clinical PACS workflows.

items.title_en: Blood lead and other metals among pregnant women in Bangladesh: national prevalence, geographic variation and household child exposure
items.abstract_en: Background. Lead crosses the placenta and harms the developing brain, and no safe level is known. Bangladesh lacks national estimates of lead exposure in pregnancy. Objectives. We estimated blood lead in pregnant women nationally, described where and in whom it was raised, and examined links with child lead and haemoglobin. Methods. In the Bangladesh Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2025, 1,932 of 2,711 eligible pregnant women (71%) had valid venous blood results. Survey-weighted modified Poisson models estimated prevalence ratios (PR) for blood lead of 3.5 microgram/dL or more, an analytical cut-off. We also studied 540 households with a tested child aged 12 to 59 months. Results. Among tested women, geometric mean blood lead was 2.05 microgram/dL (95% CI 1.99 to 2.12). In all, 17.7% (15.7 to 19.9) had 3.5 microgram/dL or more and 7.6% (6.1 to 9.3) had 5 microgram/dL or more. Greater Dhaka, defined after inspecting district estimates, held 12% of pregnant women but 64% (54 to 73) of those at 5 microgram/dL or more. The richest quintile had a crude PR of 3.06 (2.02 to 4.63, P<0.001), attenuated to 1.09 (0.72 to 1.67, P=0.678) after adjustment for place. No clear association was seen with cosmetics, indoor smoking or nearby battery sites. A woman's lead of 3.5 microgram/dL or more was associated with child lead of 5 microgram/dL or more (adjusted PR 1.50, 1.16 to 1.96, P=0.002). This cut-off identified only 23% (16 to 30) of them. Conclusions. Raised blood lead in pregnancy varied sharply by place and was highest in greater Dhaka. The crude wealth association was markedly attenuated after adjustment for place. Maternal lead was linked with child lead, but most exposed children lived with women below the cut-off. These findings support source investigation in greater Dhaka and evaluation of targeted lead assessment for women and children.

items.title_en: Introducing Infrastructure as Code for deployment and governance of medical AI: A case study
items.abstract_en: Clinical AI deployment rarely reaches the bedside because both workstation integration and governed backend provisioning are challenging. We introduce a workflow that allows rapid and governed access to AI functionalities through a browser interface or API, enabling privacy-compliant data analysis. The complex setup for compliant healthcare applications such as a secure backend, private AI model endpoint, and managed identity configuration is encoded by itself, a concept known as Infrastructure as Code (IaC). IaC is a concept in which networks, access rights, and service endpoints are written down as machine-readable files that can be reviewed once and executed identically in any institution. Here, we apply this concept to a clinical use case. The process of deploying a governed, private clinical AI solution using this approach in a tertiary care center took, on average, 310.3 +- 196.6 seconds (n=25, mean +- SD). To further demonstrate the clinical value of this approach, we developed and deployed an LLM-based inconsistency checker, which identifies textual inconsistency in medical documents. When evaluating the tool on a set of 1,347 physician-approved clinical documents, the tool flagged a clinically severe inconsistency in 105 clinical documents (7.8%, approximately 1 in 13). In a severity-stratified physician audit, 149 of 150 sampled findings were confirmed (population-weighted PPV 98.2%; CI 94.8 - 100.0). In summary, we present the application of IaC frameworks to a healthcare use case and demonstrate that clinically useful AI applications can be deployed to physician workstations in hospital-governed cloud environments within a few minutes.

items.title_en: DyssomniaNN: Multi-Scale Spiking Neural Modeling of Human Sleep Disorders and Perceived Restedness
items.title_zh: DyssomniaNN：人类睡眠障碍与感知休息感的多尺度脉冲神经建模
items.abstract_en: Clinical sleep medicine repeatedly documents profound divergences between objective sleep duration and subjective daytime impairment, notably exemplified by sleep state misperception in paradoxical insomnia and boundary instability in narcolepsy type 1. Here, we present DyssomniaNN: a multi-scale biophysical computational framework coupling Borbély's two-process regulation of sleep homeostasis and circadian drive with Saper's hypothalamic reciprocal flip-flop circuit and a recurrent corticothalamic leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neural network. We formalize five clinical cohorts across an identical 72-hour photoperiod: healthy control, circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorder (delayed-phase), chronic insomnia, paradoxical insomnia, and narcolepsy type 1. The synthetic local field potential converges closely with empirical human electroencephalography spectra from the PhysioNet Sleep-EDF database across all canonical frequency bands (spectral mean absolute error of 0.33--0.35). Furthermore, we introduce the Well-Rested Index to quantify restorative efficacy. Simulations reveal that sleep duration fails to predict restorative recovery: paradoxical insomnia achieves normal total sleep time (21.15 h) yet yields low restoration (37.6%) from unsuppressed cortical beta-band intrusion, whereas hypocretin deficiency in narcolepsy produces severe nocturnal fragmentation (781 min of wake after sleep onset) and 35 sleep-onset rapid eye movement periods. DyssomniaNN provides an in silico platform for mechanistic sleep research and virtual neuropharmacology.

items.title_en: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
items.title_zh: 用自然语言设计蛋白质结构
items.abstract_en: A central challenge in de novo protein design is generating proteins with desired structural and functional properties. Existing design models typically require a dedicated input representation for each property, limiting the design objectives they support. We develop Prompteina, the first all-atom structure generation model that supports new and broader design objectives specified in natural language, analogous to text-to-image generation. To train Prompteina, we construct Prompteina-Data, a paired text--protein structure dataset of 1.8M structures and 50M+ captions describing global and residue-specific structural and functional properties. We adapt Proteina-Complexa, a pretrained structure generation model, through text-conditioned pretraining and finetuning that aligns residues with their corresponding text. Prompteina outperforms baselines on 15 of 18 structural properties and generates proteins that more closely match descriptions of their intended functions. In binder design, it leads baselines on at least 13 of 20 targets and improves interface confidence by 14\% over the strongest baseline. With iterative in silico feedback, Prompteina's gain over non-iterative generation is 57\% larger than the next-best baseline on the hardest targets. Finally, we experimentally validate Prompteina designs against GM2A, a target with no reported de novo binders. We identify nine binders, with the strongest at an apparent $K_{\mathrm{D}}$ of 107 nM. These results establish natural language as an effective and powerful conditioning interface for protein structure generation.
items.abstract_zh: 从头蛋白质设计的一个核心挑战是生成具备所需结构与功能性质的蛋白质。现有设计模型通常要为每种性质设置专门的输入表示，限制了所能支持的设计目标。我们开发了Prompteina——首个支持以自然语言指定新的、更广泛设计目标的全原子结构生成模型，类似于文生图生成。为训练Prompteina，我们构建了Prompteina-Data：一个包含180万个结构和5000万条以上配文的文本—蛋白质结构配对数据集，配文描述了全局与残基特异性的结构及功能性质。我们通过文本条件预训练与微调（将残基与其对应文本对齐）改造了预训练结构生成模型Proteina-Complexa。Prompteina在18项结构性质中的15项上优于基线，并生成与其预期功能描述更相符的蛋白质。在结合子（binder）设计中，它在20个靶点中至少13个上领先基线，界面置信度比最强基线提升14%。借助迭代式计算机反馈，在最难靶点上，Prompteina相对非迭代生成的增益比次优基线大57%。最后，我们针对GM2A（此前无报道过的从头结合子）进行了实验验证，鉴定出9个结合子，最强者的表观KD为107 nM。这些结果确立了自然语言是蛋白质结构生成的有效而强大的条件接口。
items.highlight_zh: 首个用自然语言条件生成全原子蛋白质结构的模型
items.digest_zh:
- 研究问题：从头设计蛋白质时，想控制哪一种性质就得换一套专门的输入表示，很难灵活地同时指定多个设计目标。
- 方法：提出Prompteina，首个支持自然语言条件的全原子蛋白结构生成模型；构建Prompteina-Data数据集，含180万个结构、5000万条以上描述整体与残基层面性质的配文；在预训练模型Proteina-Complexa基础上做文本条件预训练，并微调使残基与其对应文本对齐。
- 结果：在18项结构性质中15项优于基线，生成的蛋白更符合其功能描述；结合子设计中在20个靶点里至少13个领先，界面置信度比最强基线高14%；配合迭代计算反馈，在最难靶点上的增益比次优基线大57%；实验验证针对GM2A（此前无人做出从头结合子）找到9个结合子，最强表观KD为107 nM。
- 为何重要：把“文生图”的范式搬到蛋白质设计，让自然语言成为统一、灵活的设计接口，大幅扩展了可表达的设计目标。

items.title_en: PhySeqNet: physics-informed fluorescent foci detection for BARseq spatial transcriptomics
items.title_zh: PhySeqNet：用于BARseq空间转录组学的物理信息荧光焦点检测
items.abstract_en: BARseq enables spatially resolved gene-expression profiling across intact tissue, but its sensitivity depends on accurate detection and decoding of dense fluorescent rolonies. Existing spot-calling approaches can be conservative where signals overlap, while supervised deep learning is limited by the lack of reliable manual ground truth in real tissue images. Here we present PhySeqNet, a physics-informed deep learning framework for annotation-free fluorescent foci detection in BARseq. PhySeqNet trains U-Net detectors entirely on semi-synthetic images generated from an instrument-matched optical model combined with real sample-free experimental noise, and is integrated into pyBARseq, a modular Python pipeline for BARseq analysis. PhySeqNet achieved high detection performance on held-out simulated data across wavelength bands. On real tissue images, where ground truth is unavailable, we evaluated detections by forward-model reconstruction: PhySeqNet with conservative barcode-aware non-maxima suppression (NMSB) achieved higher reconstruction fidelity (NCC and MS-SSIM) than the BarDensr single-shot estimator, tuned classical spot detectors, and a pretrained deep-learning detector. In the analyzed brain section, PhySeqNet with NMSB yielded a median of 51 counts per cell versus 47 for BarDensr, with a similar number of genes detected per cell. The recovered transcripts produced spatial expression patterns qualitatively consistent with Allen MERFISH reference data and preserved cell-type composition after scANVI label transfer. These results show that physics-informed simulation can train practical, annotation-free detectors that improve BARseq sensitivity without disrupting downstream biological interpretation.

items.title_en: RetroTAC: Learning Route-Derived Synthetic Accessibility for PROTACs
items.title_zh: RetroTAC：学习用于PROTAC的路线衍生合成可及性
items.abstract_en: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation, expanding therapeutic opportunities beyond conventional inhibition. However, assembling their large, multifunctional structures creates synthetic challenges that hinder their discovery. Traditional synthetic-accessibility scores can overestimate this difficulty by penalizing PROTACs' molecular complexity while overlooking modular assembly from accessible building blocks. In contrast, retrosynthesis planning tools provide explicit routes but are computationally expensive, particularly for large molecules. Here, we introduce a human-interpretable, PROTAC-oriented route-derived score that rewards short synthetic depth and balanced joining of molecular fragments, and RetroTAC, a machine-learning surrogate that predicts this score directly from molecular structures. RetroTAC combines complementary models in an ensemble, achieving a root mean squared error of 0.13 and an $R^2$ of 0.65 on held-out molecules. We further evaluate its utility on PROTACs enumerated by recombining warheads, linkers, and E3-ligase ligands, followed by retrosynthetic planning and route analysis. Candidates selected for high predicted scores achieve a mean route-derived synthesizability of 0.73, compared with 0.31 for low-score candidates; 98.75% versus 51.00% are fully resolved under the tested search settings. These results support RetroTAC as a fast prioritization tool for virtual PROTAC libraries, connecting molecular screening with interpretable route characteristics while reserving explicit planning for selected candidates.

items.title_en: A new device for live cell imaging of biological samples under in-plane shear
items.title_zh: 一种用于面内剪切下生物样本活细胞成像的新装置
items.abstract_en: The effect of mechanical stresses and deformations upon the behavior and properties of cells and tissues is a topic of paramount interest in the field of biophysics. Its understanding is essential for deepening our comprehension of cellular responses to environmental stimuli, with implications in fields ranging from embryogenesis to tumor development. For boosting the understanding in this field, it is important to develop devices for the application of simple deformations in order to probe the cellular response to the basic mechanical transformations. While a number of stretching devices have been developed, in-plane shearing deformation has been little investigated.
